answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a bond that is forfeited if its signed work fails a randomly sampled, independently checked task. The check ties a claim to costly output, not to a profile or reputation score that an attacker can cheaply multiply. A sparrow agent may wander among tasks, but creating thousands of identities still requires locking capital in every bond; coordinated fakes risk losing those bonds when delta checks expose copied or invalid work.
